es.summary: Enfermedad autoinmune crónica que produce inflamación y daño multisistémico, afectando piel, articulaciones, riñones, corazón, pulmones y cerebro.
key_points: ANA y anti‑dsDNA positivos son marcadores diagnósticos.
Daño renal (nefritis) es la complicación más grave.
El tratamiento combina antiinflamatorios, antipalúdicos y corticoides.
Protección solar y evitar desencadenantes reducen brotes.

pathophysiology: Autoanticuerpos contra componentes nucleares forman complejos inmunes.
Los complejos se depositan en vasos, activan complemento y causan inflamación.
Daño tisular crónico afecta piel, articulaciones, riñón, corazón y CNS.
diagnostics: Creatinina y proteinuria para evaluar riñón.
treatment: Corticoides sistémicos o tópicos según gravedad.
nursing_care: Evaluar dolor articular, erupción y nivel de energía cada turno.
Monitorear presión arterial, frecuencia cardíaca y signos de edema.
Controlar laboratorio: CBC, creatinina, proteinuria, complemento.
Administrar medicamentos según orden y observar efectos adversos.
patient_teaching: Uso diario de protector solar SPF 30+ y ropa protectora.
Tomar hidroxicloroquina sin interrupción y reportar visión borrosa.
Reconocer signos de infección o brote y buscar atención inmediata.
Mantener dieta balanceada y ejercicio moderado según tolerancia.

evidenced_by: cansancio al realizar actividades de la vida diaria
disminución de la tolerancia al ejercicio
outcomes: Aumenta la tolerancia a la actividad para realizar ADL sin fatiga excesiva en 2 semanas
Mantiene nivel de energía ≥7/10 en escala de 0‑10

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de fatiga y capacidad funcional usando escala de Borg cada turno
interventions.rationale: Permite identificar cambios y planificar actividades adecuadas

interventions.action: Programar descansos programados y actividades de bajo impacto
interventions.rationale: Reduce la sobrecarga muscular y mejora la tolerancia

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de conservación de energía (sentarse al vestirse, dividir tareas)
interventions.rationale: Facilita la realización de ADL sin exacerbar síntomas

interventions.action: Coordinar con fisioterapia para plan de ejercicio progresivo
interventions.rationale: Mejora la fuerza y la resistencia de forma segura

interventions.action: Monitorear signos vitales antes y después de la actividad

outcomes: No presenta signos de infección durante la hospitalización

interventions.action: Realizar higiene de manos antes y después de cada contacto
Evaluar temperatura, sitio de inserción de catéter y secreciones cada turno
Mantener aislamiento estándar y usar guantes cuando sea necesario
Educar al paciente sobre signos de infección y cuándo buscar ayuda
interventions.rationale: Promueve detección precoz y tratamiento oportuno

interventions.action: Revisar y registrar cumplimiento de vacunación (influenza, neumococo)

en.summary: Chronic autoimmune disease that causes inflammation and multisystem damage, affecting skin, joints, kidneys, heart, lungs, and brain.
key_points: Positive ANA and anti‑dsDNA are diagnostic markers.
Renal damage (nephritis) is the most serious complication.
Treatment combines anti‑inflammatories, antimalarials, and corticosteroids.
Sun protection and avoiding triggers reduce flares.

pathophysiology: Autoantibodies against nuclear components form immune complexes.
The complexes deposit in vessels, activate complement, and cause inflammation.
Chronic tissue damage affects skin, joints, kidney, heart, and CNS.
diagnostics: Creatinine and proteinuria to assess kidney function.
treatment: Systemic or topical corticosteroids as needed.
nursing_care: Assess joint pain, rash, and energy level each shift.
Monitor blood pressure, heart rate, and signs of edema.
Track labs: CBC, creatinine, proteinuria, complement.
Administer medications per order and observe for adverse effects.
patient_teaching: Use daily sunscreen SPF 30+ and protective clothing.
Take hydroxychloroquine consistently and report blurred vision.
Recognize signs of infection or flare and seek immediate care.
Maintain a balanced diet and moderate exercise as tolerated.

evidenced_by: tiredness during activities of daily living
outcomes: Increase activity tolerance to perform ADLs without excessive fatigue in 2 weeks
Maintain energy level ≥7/10 on a 0‑10 scale

interventions.action: Assess fatigue level and functional capacity using the Borg scale each shift
interventions.rationale: Allows identification of changes and planning of appropriate activities

interventions.action: Schedule planned rest periods and low‑impact activities
interventions.rationale: Reduces muscular overload and improves tolerance

interventions.action: Teach energy conservation techniques (sit while dressing, break tasks into smaller steps)
interventions.rationale: Facilitates ADL performance without exacerbating symptoms

interventions.action: Coordinate with physical therapy for a progressive exercise plan
Monitor vital signs before and after activity

outcomes: No signs of infection during hospitalization
Maintain temperature <38 °C and normal leukocyte count

interventions.action: Perform hand hygiene before and after each contact
Assess temperature, catheter insertion site, and secretions each shift
Maintain standard isolation and use gloves when necessary
Educate patient on signs of infection and when to seek help
interventions.rationale: Promotes early detection and timely treatment

interventions.action: Review and document vaccination status (influenza, pneumococcal)

summary.0.quote: This attack causes inflammation. It can also damage many parts of the body, including the joints, skin, kidneys, heart, lungs, and brain.

sections.pathophysiology.2.quote: It can also damage many parts of the body, including the joints, skin, kidneys, heart, lungs, and brain.

sections.risk_factors.3.quote: Drug-induced lupus is caused by a reaction to some medicines.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: It causes a rash or sores, usually after your skin is exposed to sunlight .

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: Fever Fatigue or feeling tired often

sections.complications.2.quote: Heart problems , including inflammation in the heart (myocarditis), heart valves , or lining of the heart muscle ( pericarditis ).

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: May order blood tests, such as ANA (antinuclear antibody) , antibodies, complete blood count , and complement tests May order other tests, such as urine tests

sections.patient_teaching.2.quote: It helps to learn more about lupus - being able to spot the warning signs of a flare can help you prevent the flare or make the symptoms less severe.
